SOURCE: "Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation" (CRAG), Shi-Qi Yan, Jia-Chen Gu, Yun Zhu, Zhen-Hua Ling (USTC, UCLA, Google DeepMind). arXiv:2401.15884v3, 7 Oct 2024. The PDF header names no venue, so treat it as an arXiv preprint. Code: github.com/HuskyInSalt/CRAG.

COVERAGE: 61,371 of 61,371 chars read (all pages: body, Tables 1-6, Appendix A prompts, B.1-B.5, Table 11). References were skimmed only. Extraction was clean. I did not run the figure-captions script. Figure 1-3 captions came from the text.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. A small fine-tuned evaluator classifies retrieval quality better than prompted ChatGPT.
- number: 84.3 vs 58.0 / 62.4 / 64.7
- setup: PopQA retrieval results. Evaluator is T5-large, 0.77B, fine-tuned. The ChatGPT baselines are GPT-3.5 Turbo (direct, CoT, few-shot). Metric is evaluator accuracy.
- quote: "Our Retrieval Evaluator (T5-based) 84.3 / ChatGPT 58.0 / ChatGPT-CoT 62.4 / ChatGPT-few-shot 64.7"
- where: Table 4, section 5.5 (about 28k chars in)
2. CRAG improves standard RAG on all four datasets.
- number: with SelfRAG-LLaMA2-7b, PopQA 52.8 -> 59.8, Bio FactScore 59.2 -> 74.1, PubHealth 39.0 -> 75.6, ARC 53.2 -> 68.6. With LLaMA2-hf-7b, PopQA 50.5 -> 54.9, Bio 44.9 -> 47.7, Pub 48.9 -> 59.5, ARC 43.4 -> 53.7.
- setup: Same Contriever retrievals as Self-RAG, so results are comparable. Accuracy, except Biography, which uses FactScore. PopQA is the 1,399-query long-tail subset.
- quote: "CRAG outperformed RAG by margins of 7.0% accuracy on PopQA, 14.9% FactScore on Biography, 36.6% accuracy on PubHealth, and 15.4% accuracy on Arc-Challenge when based on SelfRAG-LLaMA2-7b, as well as by margins of 4.4% accuracy on PopQA, 2.8% FactScore on Biography, and 10.3% on Arc-Challenge when based on LLaMA2-hf-7b."
- where: Table 1, section 5.3
- Note: the paper says "margins of 7.0%" etc. but these are absolute points (52.8 to 59.8). The PubHealth gain for hf-7b (48.9 to 59.5) is not in the quoted text.
3. Self-CRAG beats Self-RAG, and Self-RAG breaks when you swap in a generator that was not instruction-tuned for it.
- number: SelfRAG-7b: PopQA 54.9 -> 61.8, Bio 81.2 -> 86.2, Pub 72.4 -> 74.8, ARC 67.3 vs 67.2 (no gain). With LLaMA2-hf-7b: Self-RAG* 29.0 / 32.2 / 0.7 / 23.9, Self-CRAG 49.0 / 69.1 / 0.6 / 27.9.
- quote: "Compared with the current state-of-the-art Self-RAG, Self-CRAG outperformed it by margins of 20.0% accuracy on PopQA, 36.9% FactScore on Biography, and 4.0% accuracy on Arc-Challenge when based on LLaMA2-hf-7b"
- where: Table 1, section 5.3. The Self-RAG* numbers were reproduced by the authors.
4. Ablation of the three actions on PopQA: removing any one action lowers accuracy.
- number: CRAG on hf-7b: 54.9 full, 53.2 without Correct, 54.4 without Incorrect, 54.0 without Ambiguous. On SelfRAG-7b: 59.8 full, 58.3 / 59.5 / 59.0. Self-CRAG on hf-7b: 49.0 full, 43.6 / 47.7 / 48.1.
- quote: "w/o. Correct 53.2 58.3 / w/o. Incorrect 54.4 59.5 / w/o. Ambiguous 54.0 59.0"
- where: Table 2
- Single-action-only runs (Table 11, appendix): CRAG hf-7b 54.9 full, only Correct 52.4, only Incorrect 47.0, only Ambiguous 52.7. SelfRAG-7b 59.8 full, 56.7 / 48.5 / 58.0. Forcing web-only (Incorrect) is the worst.
- The Ambiguous action reduces dependence on evaluator accuracy: "Preliminary experiments of employing only the Correct and Incorrect actions show that the efficacy of CRAG was easily affected by the accuracy of the retrieval evaluator."
5. Ablation of knowledge-utilisation steps (PopQA accuracy): refinement, query rewriting and selection each help. Selection matters most for Self-CRAG on hf-7b.
- number: CRAG hf-7b 54.9 full, 49.8 without refinement, 51.7 without rewriting, 50.9 without selection. SelfRAG-7b 59.8 full, 54.2 / 56.2 / 58.6. Self-CRAG hf-7b 49.0 full, 35.9 / 37.2 / 24.9. Self-CRAG SelfRAG-7b 61.8 full, 52.2 / 58.4 / 57.9.
- quote: "w/o. refinement 49.8 54.2 / w/o. rewriting 51.7 56.2 / w/o. selection 50.9 58.6"
- where: Table 3
6. The gain comes from the correction mechanism, not just from adding web search.
- number: PopQA, hf-7b: CRAG 54.9, RAG 50.5, RAG w. web 52.2. SelfRAG-7b: CRAG 59.8, RAG 52.8, RAG w. web 53.8. Self-RAG 54.9, Self-RAG w. web 57.9, Self-CRAG 61.8. On hf-7b, Self-RAG 29.0, Self-RAG w. web 24.9, Self-CRAG 49.0.
- quote: "RAG w. web 52.2 53.8" and "augmenting RAG or Self-RAG with the proposed self-correction mechanism significantly outperformed the models consistently supplemented with web search knowledge in all cases."
- where: Table 5, section 5.7
7. Overhead is modest. This is a rough estimate of the generation phase only.
- number: TFLOPs per token 26.5 (RAG) vs 27.2 (CRAG). Execution time per instance 0.363s (RAG) vs 0.512s (CRAG). Self-RAG 0.741s, Self-CRAG 0.908s.
- setup: PopQA, A800 GPU. Retrieval and data-processing stages (including web search latency) are excluded.
- quote: "TFLOPs per token executing time(s) / RAG 26.5 0.363 / CRAG 27.2 0.512 / Self-RAG 26.5 ∼132.4 0.741 / Self-CRAG 27.2 ∼80.2 0.908"
- where: Table 6, section 5.8
8. Robustness to a degraded retriever (Figure 3): accurate retrievals were removed at random on PopQA with SelfRAG-LLaMA-7b. Self-CRAG degraded more slowly than Self-RAG. The actual retrieval accuracy was 69.8.
- number: 69.8 (actual retrieval accuracy). The paper gives no other exact figures, only a plot.
- quote: "as the retrieval performance dropped, the generation performance of Self-CRAG dropped more slightly than that of Self-RAG."
- where: section 5.6, Figure 3

Method and settings (for the note's CRAG description)
- Evaluator: T5-large, scores each (question, document) pair separately, about 10 docs per question, in the range -1 to 1. Labels are +1 and -1, from PopQA gold wiki titles, with negatives sampled from retrieved results.
- Correct: at least one document is above the upper threshold. The documents go to decompose-filter-recompose.
- Incorrect: all documents are below the lower threshold. Retrieved documents are discarded and the system uses web search.
- Ambiguous: everything else. It uses both internal and web knowledge.
- Thresholds were "set empirically", per dataset, as (upper, lower): PopQA (0.59, -0.99), PubHealth/ARC (0.5, -0.91), Biography (0.95, -0.91).
- Strip filter: top-5 strips, filter threshold -0.5. Web: Google Search API, top-5, Wikipedia preferred. Queries are rewritten into at most three keywords by GPT-3.5 Turbo (few-shot prompt, Table 7).
- quote: "The two confidence thresholds for triggering one of the three actions were set empirically." (App. B.3)
- The evaluator was fine-tuned on PopQA training data (the roughly 14k samples minus the 1,399 test queries) and transferred unchanged to Bio, Pub and ARC.

LIMITS
- The authors concede: "fine-tuning an external retrieval evaluator is inevitable." Removing it is left to future work.
- All generators are LLaMA2-7B variants. No stronger LLM generators were tested.
- The evaluator is trained on PopQA signals, and the thresholds are tuned per dataset. Whether a threshold generalises is not shown.
- The paper gives no latency figure that includes retrieval or web search. Table 6 covers generation only.
- No confidence intervals and no seeds are reported. Many deltas are small (CRAG without Incorrect is 0.5 below on PopQA, 54.9 vs 54.4).
- Web search is a live commercial API (Google), so results may not be reproducible. Biases from web content are only mitigated by preferring Wikipedia.
- PubHealth with hf-7b gives near-zero scores for Self-RAG and Self-CRAG (0.7 and 0.6). The authors blame instruction-following failure ("fail to generate True or False").
- Relevance to the target note: the paper does not test a confidence-gate threshold of 0.7 or a Bedrock KB. It shows nothing about how often the gate short-circuits, and nothing about CRAG on enterprise or support corpora.
- Dated: LLaMA2-era models and Contriever retrieval.

BUILDS ON: Lewis et al., 2020 (RAG); Asai et al., 2024 (Self-RAG, also the source of the retrieval results and PopQA split); Raffel et al., 2020 (T5); Izacard et al., 2022 (Contriever); Mallen et al., 2023 (PopQA); Min et al., 2023 (FactScore/Biography); Zhang et al., 2023a (PubHealth); Bhakthavatsalam et al., 2021 (ARC); Luo et al., 2023 (SAIL); Dhuliawala et al., 2024 (CoVe); Narayanan et al., 2021 (FLOPs formulas); Piktus et al., 2021 and Komeili et al., 2022 (web search augmentation).

CODE: no code in the paper. Algorithm 1 (CRAG Inference) is pseudocode in section 4.2: score each (x, d_i) with the evaluator E, then produce a Confidence value. CORRECT gives k = Knowledge_Refine(x, D). INCORRECT gives k = Web_Search(W rewrites x). AMBIGUOUS gives k = both. Then G predicts y given x and k. The prompts in Appendix A are worth reusing (Table 8, direct yes/no relevance grader: "Given a question, does the following document have exact information to answer the question? Answer yes or no only.").

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p1): low-quality retriever examples (Henry Feilden, Death of a Batman) where a wrong document leads to a wrong answer.
- Fig 2 (p4): inference flow. Evaluator -> Correct / Ambiguous / Incorrect -> refine / rewrite + web search -> generator. This is the best single picture of the method.
- Fig 3 (p7): generation accuracy vs retrieval accuracy for Self-RAG and Self-CRAG on PopQA.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Table text layout in the extraction is flattened but the values read unambiguously. The Table 1 column order is PopQA, Bio, Pub, ARC. Table 1's "Self-RAG*" row under LLaMA2-hf-7b was reproduced by the authors. Check the note's claims about the "CRAG +0.005 MRR, 0.7 gate" and the "LangGraph graph agent with CRAG" against the source. The paper's CRAG is a trained T5 evaluator with web fallback and strip refinement. A LangGraph CRAG with a 0.7 gate on Bedrock scores is a re-implementation, not the paper's method, and the paper does not report MRR or P@1.
